docs.text: U.S. Agricultural Commodity Prices Across Business Cycles Project type: Exploratory empirical analysis and data visualization Crops: Corn, soybeans, wheat Historical coverage described in essay: approximately 1995–2025 Methods: USDA-derived price data, FRED macroeconomic series, MySQL/Python processing, iterative imputation, crop- and regime-specific OLS with HAC standard errors, residual diagnostics, Power BI. Research question How do the statistical associations between U.S. agricultural prices and macroeconomic variables vary across four Merrill-clock economic regimes, and do these patterns differ across crops? Research workflow Gather local USDA-derived crop price CSV and FRED macroeconomic series. Load and query crop records through MySQL; standardize dates and merge monthly data. Audit missing observations and compare price distributions. Impute explanatory variables using IterativeImputer(random_state=42) (default estimator: BayesianRidge). Construct regime labels from industrial production and CPI movements. Estimate OLS regressions by crop and regime with Newey–West HAC standard errors (12 lags in supplied code). Examine residual dependence (Durbin–Watson, ACF, Ljung–Box) and rolling/event-split sensitivity. Export result tables to Excel and visualize in Power BI. What this site is — and is not This documentation reconstructs the reported workflow from the essay and the researcher's stated experience. It is not a full executable reproduction because the original USDA extraction request, full dataset, SQL history, intermediate experiments, and verification logs are not supplied here. Do not interpret pseudocode or recommended checks as evidence they were already executed. Current status: The cycle-specific results and dashboard are original exploratory outputs. A possible time-alignment problem in the year-over-year regime indicators has been identified but not corrected or re-estimated . Evidence provenance USDA NASS Quick Stats — official agricultural price data portal. FRED — macroeconomic series ( MCOILWTICO , FEDFUNDS , TWEXB , CPIAUCSL , INDPRO ). docs.text: Model diagnostics and robustness Residual autocorrelation The essay reports full-sample Durbin–Watson statistics of 0.229 for corn, 0.231 for soybeans, and 0.313 for wheat . Residual ACF and Ljung–Box diagnostics likewise raise concerns about serial dependence. Newey–West HAC standard errors help adjust inference for dependence but do not eliminate autocorrelation or fix missing dynamic structure. Rolling-window sensitivity The study plots the WTI_DROUGHT coefficient with 48-, 60- and 72-month windows. Central patterns are sometimes similar, but sharp spikes and sign changes near event boundaries suggest sensitivity to window composition. Limited variation in the drought dummy within a rolling window can make an interaction poorly identified. Event-split sensitivity Before/after comparisons cover RFS, 2012 drought, trade war, COVID-19 and Russia–Ukraine conflict. The essay notes very large RFS coefficient differences, which should not be interpreted as causal policy effects: a dummy may have no variation on one side of an event cutoff. Future tests — not completed Add lagged dependent and macroeconomic terms and reassess residual dependence. Report uncertainty intervals and identification flags for rolling coefficients. Use comparable pre/post windows and avoid plotting unidentifiable coefficients as zero. Test cross-regime differences formally in a correctly specified pooled model.

docs.text: Missing-data investigation and imputation Reported data audit The essay reports 1,137 crop–month records: 379 per crop. USD_INDEX is missing in 1,017 rows (89.4%), WTI and FFR in 36 each (3.2%), and CPI in 39 (3.4%). The crop prices themselves were not imputed. Only 40 records per crop were complete across regression variables, so complete-case deletion would discard most observations. The researcher compared missingness with histograms, a full-panel heatmap, and crop-specific price distribution/boxplots using ±1σ, ±2σ, and ±3σ ranges. Most rows with missing explanatory variables had ordinary, not extreme, crop-price values. This does not prove missing-at-random. Actual imputation method The supplied code calls: imputer = IterativeImputer(random_state=42) Because no estimator= argument is passed, scikit-learn's default conditional estimator is BayesianRidge . The procedure iteratively fills missing explanatory variables and returns a single completed dataset in this implementation. The final crop-price regressions are OLS , not Bayesian ridge regressions. This is not pooled multiple-imputation inference. Challenge and trade-off The main technical problem was preserving sample coverage without silently assuming the missing data were harmless. Imputation made the models estimable, but with 89.4% of dollar-index entries imputed, dollar-related coefficient interpretation is highly assumption-dependent. Recommended but not yet demonstrated: re-estimate models excluding USD_INDEX , compare alternative imputation strategies, and report sensitivity of coefficient signs and intervals. Never label these proposed checks as completed tests.

docs.text: Data acquisition, MySQL and integration Goal and inputs The study uses three crop-price series loaded from a local crop_price.csv attributed to USDA NASS, together with FRED macroeconomic series. The essay states 379 observations per crop (1,137 crop–month rows), although the effective model sample may differ because FRED retrieval begins in January 1996 and regime classification excludes some dates. Input Role Verification still needed USDA-derived crop price CSV Dependent variable price ; crop/date keys Exact NASS query, units, original download date FRED MCOILWTICO WTI oil price Aggregation of daily to monthly frequency FRED FEDFUNDS Federal funds rate Frequency and alignment FRED TWEXB Trade-weighted dollar index Sparse overlap and historical coverage FRED CPIAUCSL CPI/inflation proxy Date-level YoY construction FRED INDPRO Industrial production/growth proxy Date-level YoY construction Technical challenge: learning SQL and connecting Python to MySQL Challenge (researcher-reported): I was initially unfamiliar with SQL syntax and database connection setup. Moving a local CSV into MySQL and then using Python to retrieve the records introduced several practical difficulties: connection configuration, matching column types, checking dates, and joining data from different sources. Process to document honestly: 1. Identify the required database fields: date , commodity_desc , price . 2. Create or inspect a table with compatible date and numeric types. 3. Import crop-price rows and check the number of records by crop. 4. Use a Python database client to query records into pandas. 5. Merge monthly macroeconomic data by date; check unmatched dates and duplicate keys. 6. Compare SQL counts against pandas counts to detect accidental duplication. The following is an illustrative verification query , not a preserved query from the original project: SELECT commodity_desc, COUNT(*) AS observations, MIN(date) AS first_month, MAX(date) AS last_month FROM crop_prices GROUP BY commodity_desc; And a suggested pandas merge check: assert df_crop[['date', 'commodity_desc']].duplicated().sum() == 0 assert df_macro['date'].duplicated().sum() == 0 panel = df_crop.merge(df_macro, on='date', how='left', validate='many_to_one') print(panel.groupby('commodity_desc').size()) Lessons learned: A successful database connection is not the same as a correct analytical dataset. Row counts, join cardinality, date formats, units and frequency must all be verified before modeling. Credential safety Do not publish database passwords, FRED API tokens or other credentials in a public repository. Replace them with environment variables and rotate any secrets previously exposed. Provide a .env.example containing placeholder names, never real values.

docs.text: Regression design, interactions and multicollinearity Baseline analytical approach The essay reports separate OLS regressions for corn, soybeans and wheat, and additional regressions within Merrill-clock regimes. HAC/Newey–West standard errors use maxlags=12 in the supplied code. Coefficients describe conditional associations , not causal impacts. Technical difficulty: too many interaction variables Researcher-reported experiment: I initially constructed interaction variables between Merrill-clock economic-regime indicators and macroeconomic explanatory variables, hoping to allow the oil-price, interest-rate and dollar-price relationships to differ across cycles. The resulting specification suffered from multicollinearity/numerical instability. I removed the broad set of cycle-by-macro interaction terms and used separate regressions for each regime in the reported analysis. Why the experimental interaction specification was still linear regression An interaction between a regime dummy and a macroeconomic variable does not make the model nonlinear in its coefficients. For example, the experimental specification [P_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_t + \beta_2 D_t + \beta_3(X_t D_t) + \varepsilon_t] is linear in the parameters and can be estimated by OLS. Here D is a regime indicator. This example illustrates the attempted idea; it is not the final estimated specification . In a pooled regression, one regime should serve as the reference when including an intercept. Redundant dummy coding or interacting variables within a single-regime subset can create exact collinearity. Final reported approach The final essay reports separate OLS linear regressions by crop and by economic regime , with Newey–West HAC standard errors ( maxlags=12 ). Broad regime-by-macro interactions were removed after multicollinearity concerns. Two targeted interactions, WTI_DROUGHT and FFR_SEASON , remained in the documented model. HAC changes standard-error estimation, not the linear OLS coefficient specification. What changed Design stage Intended benefit Difficulty / decision Pooled OLS with macro regressors Baseline conditional relationships Retained as a comparison Broad cycle × macro interactions Directly model cycle-dependent slopes Researcher reports multicollinearity; broad interactions removed Separate OLS per regime and crop Easier to describe within-regime patterns Retained, but small and unequal samples limit reliability WTI_DROUGHT and FFR_SEASON Specific oil–drought and rate–season interactions Retained in the essay; do not claim all interaction terms were deleted Important precision The original experimental model output, variance inflation factors, design-matrix rank, and exact deleted variable list are not preserved in the supplied essay . Therefore, the documentation should say the researcher encountered multicollinearity and revised the specification, not invent VIF numbers, error messages, or quantitative improvements. Recommended reproducibility diagnostics (not yet verified) import numpy as np from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor X = model_matrix.dropna().astype(float) print('rank:', np.linalg.matrix_rank(X), 'columns:', X.shape[1]) print('condition number:', np.linalg.cond(X)) vifs = {name: variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i) for i, name in enumerate(X.columns)} print(vifs) Interpret VIF and condition numbers with context; multicollinearity may reflect deterministic dummy coding, insufficient variation or correlated regressors. Removing interactions simplifies estimation but sacrifices direct pooled tests of slope differences. Separate-regime significance patterns do not by themselves establish that coefficients differ statistically between regimes. Other identification challenges Recovery has 9 observations per crop and recession 21, compared with 242 in overheating and 91 in stagflation. Event dummies with no within-regime variation cannot be identified. Treat very large or highly significant estimates in tiny subsamples with caution.

docs.text: Limitations and open validation work Critical unresolved issue: time alignment of economic-cycle indicators The code review identified that year-over-year changes for INDPRO and CPI were computed using pct_change(12) after macroeconomic observations were merged into a crop-level panel. Since a month can appear once per crop, a 12-row shift can be approximately a four-month shift when there are three crop rows per month, rather than a twelve-month change. Status: This issue has been identified and disclosed; the date-level indicators and resulting regime assignments have not been recomputed or independently validated . Therefore, the current cycle counts, cycle-specific regressions, significance tests, and dashboard cycle comparisons must be treated as exploratory outputs. Proposed repair, not executed in the present research deliverable monthly = (df_macro[['date', 'INDPRO', 'CPI']] .drop_duplicates('date') .sort_values('date') .copy()) monthly['INDPRO_yoy'] = monthly['INDPRO'].pct_change(12) * 100 monthly['CPI_yoy'] = monthly['CPI'].pct_change(12) * 100 panel = df_crop.merge(monthly, on='date', how='left', validate='many_to_one') # Recreate regime labels, rerun regression/diagnostics, update Excel and Power BI. Before using a 12-row lag even on monthly data, verify consecutive monthly dates, no duplicates and the exact intended growth/inflation definitions. Other limitations Issue Evidence Consequence Regime imbalance 9 recovery vs 242 overheating observations per crop Underpowered or unstable regime estimates Dollar-index missingness 1,017 / 1,137 values imputed Dollar coefficients depend heavily on model assumptions Serial dependence DW 0.229 / 0.231 / 0.313 and residual ACF Model dynamics may be incomplete Event-dummy identification Some events absent within subsamples Coefficients may be unidentified or misleading Data provenance Original USDA CSV query not supplied Units and exact source filters need verification Validation checklist [ ] Confirm exact USDA Quick Stats series, units and extraction date. [ ] Verify all monthly keys and source-frequency transformations. [ ] Recalculate macroeconomic changes on unique monthly dates. [ ] Compare original and corrected regime labels. [ ] Rerun affected cycle regressions, diagnostics and sensitivity analyses. [ ] Evaluate imputation sensitivity without the dollar index. [ ] Refresh Power BI Excel inputs while preserving schema.
